1#_: (Siman 102 seif 1 in the hagahah) However, if one whitened it in food or placed it in a pot to fix, it is not nullified. The reason poskim wrote: everything that needs one another is called for this purpose its kind, like water and salt in dough stated in the Gemara and poskim at the end of Beitzah (daf 39) and in Orach Chayim siman 513 — see there at length.
2#_: (Seif 3) A vessel that became forbidden through absorption of prohibition and was mixed — it is nullified in the majority and we do not judge it like something that has a permitted aspect. This is specifically that it absorbed a prohibition that has no permitted aspect — it is not like something that has a permitted aspect what becomes permitted through hagalah, because one must expend outlay, etc.; but a vessel that absorbed a prohibition that has a permitted aspect — see Shach and poskim.
3#_: (Seif 4 in the hagahah) One who vowed from one matter and it was mixed afterward. See in Peri Megadim in the introduction to Laws of Yom Tov who wrote: one who vowed benefit and it was mixed — one can say it is nullified, for when we say something that has a permitted aspect is not nullified, that is for eating, not for benefit; and likewise for moving one can say it is nullified — see there; and so Tzelach: granted for eating and benefit, but for moving, etc. — see there.
4#_: (There in the hagahah) If it remains forbidden for one forever even though permitted for others, such as one who cooks on Shabbat — it is not called something that has a permitted aspect. And see Magen Avraham in Orach Chayim siman 318 — it deals with mixing after Shabbat; for if on Shabbat it is literally something that has a permitted aspect after Shabbat relative to others; and similarly regarding what is written in siman 318 — see there.
